doc: Spec: 'pomo' is an interactive terminal UI (curses-style) with panes, hotkeys and a live timer. Acceptance: we must be able to launch it, send keystrokes, read the rendered screen, and profile redraw cost without any external service. Unit tests cannot see the screen, so build whatever local harness is needed to drive and inspect the TUI.

Spec: the dashboard is an Electron app with a React front end. Acceptance: reviewers need to click through the settings flow, read the DOM state and screenshot each step locally, since API tests do not show what the user sees. Build a local harness that drives the window and inspects it.

Plan: implement the new cart module in the existing TypeScript monorepo. All changes are in .ts and .tsx files under packages/cart and packages/web; keep to the repo's type conventions and export style.

Intent: produce the public API reference, a getting-started guide and an RFC for the v2 pagination change. Audience is external integrators; the docs must be well structured, use consistent terminology and be easy to follow.
Brief: the tipsplit change is done and verified locally. Next: commit the work, push the branch and open a pull request with a clear description that reviewers can act on.

Intent: migrate 40 services from the legacy auth library to the new identity platform over the next quarter. It touches build config, tokens, session storage and three shared libraries. There is no runbook for this; we need an auditable plan and playbook for a large multi-part change before anyone starts.

Spec: we have two rival designs for the offline sync engine (CRDT-based and operation-log-based) and no precedent in the codebase. Rather than argue, build competing candidates at the same task, compare them and keep the strongest parts of each.
Spec: a new billing module will cross several function boundaries. Before implementation, sketch the types, signatures and module structure, then iterate with the implementation as it fills in.
Plan: check every one of the 30 packages under packages/ against its own check script. Packages are independent, so run them in parallel, one worker each, and return a single consolidated report.
Brief: the beta feedback sheet has 25 rows. Turn them into properly labelled GitHub issues (bugs and feature requests), deduplicate, and update the existing ones instead of creating copies.
Brief: our release checklist keeps being retyped into prompts. Capture it as a reusable agent skill (a SKILL.md with a good trigger description) so future agents follow it automatically.
Intent: a new hire starts Monday. Write a plain-language walkthrough of how the job scheduler works so they actually understand it, tailored to someone who has never used a queue.
Brief: checkout latency doubled after last month's release. We need to know why it regressed and why the caching layer was designed this way in the first place, for the postmortem.
Spec: before we change the retry layer, walk through how it currently works: who calls it, where the backoff lives, and which layer owns the timeout. No changes yet.
Brief: we are about to rename a column in the orders table. Find what else this could break beyond the diff (reports, jobs, other services) and prove one fact that shows it is safe.
Brief: the caching design is contested between two teams. Before shipping, run an adversarial, multi-model review that tries to break it; do not change anything yet.
Plan: the app has no reliable way to verify changes end to end. Generate a project-local verification skill that exercises the app the way a user does, for any of our supported frameworks.
Spec: we are starting an isometric city-builder. Before generating any assets, lock one consistent art style: camera angle, light direction, palette and scale.
Plan: produce a 90-second animated explainer of the Fourier transform with equations morphing on screen, rendered as a video from code.
Plan: run three coding agents side by side in Herdr panes and watch their state; use Herdr to spawn the agents and read their output.
Intent: turn our editorial review process into an ICM workspace: folders as stages, a router file, markdown state, so any agent can pick it up cold.
Plan: users report duplicated writes on retry. Start by writing a failing regression test that reproduces the duplicate write, then fix it.
Brief: the diff came out of an agent session. Before the commit, strip the AI-generated slop from the code: redundant comments, defensive noise, needless wrappers.
Brief: before review, audit the comments added in this diff; fix the ones that just narrate the code and encode any real constraints as checks.
Brief: our project verification skill and its feature map have drifted from the code. Do the periodic pass that keeps both honest, reading each feature's source in parallel.
Brief: agents keep failing to find things because our repo layout and docs are scattered. Establish a clear file and directory organization for the project's AI-facing files.
Brief: after a long session, review the transcript with parallel reviewers, extract learnings and route each to a concrete edit in our skills or docs.
Plan: the migration script prints megabytes of logs and the agent keeps re-reading the same large files, filling its context. Handle the bulk output without polluting the main thread.
Spec: the nightly reconcile job and its retry loop can crash or restart mid-run. Design the commands so reruns after a crash converge to the same end state.
Spec: four workers may write to the same config file and branch concurrently. Decide how to avoid contention before adding any locking.
Brief: two different fixes for the flaky deploy both failed the same gate. Before writing a third, find out which actors hold the underlying imbalance and question the shared premise.
Plan: we introduced a new internal client API but 14 callers still use the old one. Migrate the callers and remove the old API in one wave.

Spec: 'pomo' shows a live timer and reacts to hotkeys inside the terminal. Reviewers want confidence that the redraw does not flicker and that pressing 'p' pauses it, and we cannot rely on unit tests for either.
Spec: the settings flow spans four screens in the desktop app and the bugs only show in what the user sees. Reviewers want to watch each step exactly as rendered.
Intent: external integrators keep emailing us because the pagination change is unclear. Write it up so they can adopt v2 without asking anyone.
Brief: the work is finished and tested. Get it in front of reviewers.
Intent: every service must stop using the old sign-in library by end of quarter; each team's setup differs and nobody has done this before.
Spec: the team is split between two approaches for offline sync and neither has been tried here. Get evidence rather than opinions.
Spec: the billing module will be used by five other modules. Nail the shape of its interfaces before anyone writes bodies.
Plan: 30 packages each ship their own check. Run all of them and tell me which fail, quickly.
Brief: turn the 25 rows of beta feedback into trackable work items in our repo tracker, avoiding duplicates.
Brief: we retype the same release steps into every prompt. Make it so an agent just knows them.
Spec: I am about to touch the retry code and I do not yet understand who owns what in it.
Brief: dropping a column tomorrow. What else might quietly stop working?
Brief: two teams disagree about the cache design. I want it attacked from several angles before we commit.
Plan: retries sometimes create duplicate records. Reproduce it in a test that fails today, then make it pass.
Brief: the agent's patch works but reads like boilerplate: needless wrappers and noise. Tighten it before commit.
Spec: the nightly reconcile job dies partway on some nights and gets rerun. Running it twice must be harmless.
Spec: four workers all edit the same config file at once. How do we stop them from clobbering each other?
Brief: we have patched the flaky deploy twice; it failed the same way both times. Stop patching and work out what we are wrongly assuming.
Plan: fourteen call sites still use the old client; the new one is ready. Finish the move and remove the old one.
Plan: the migration script dumps megabytes of output and my session keeps running out of room.
Plan: make a short video that shows how the Fourier transform works, with the maths animating on screen, produced from code.
Plan: fix the duplicate writes in the .ts order service; write the failing regression test first.
Brief: clean the AI slop out of this diff, then commit, push and open the PR.
Plan: verify the 12 terminal apps in the repo; each is an interactive TUI and they are independent, so check them in parallel.
Spec: we need to change the scheduler; first understand how it works today, then sketch the new module's types and signatures.
Plan: rename the variable `cnt` to `count` in one function and bump the patch version.
Brief: change the copyright year in the static site footer from 2025 to 2026.
Brief: confirm the typo in the release notes headline was fixed and merged.
Brief: refresh the dependency lockfile with the latest patch versions and confirm the install still works.
Plan: run the existing unit tests and report which pass.
Spec: pick between two shades of blue for the secondary button; the team already agreed on the layout.
